summary: Shows running ad hoc commands asynchronously with `-B` (timeout) and `-P` (poll interval), checking a background job with `async_status` and its job ID, and polling automatically. All jobs start before polling begins, the process is killed when `-B` expires, and async suits long shell commands or upgrades, not copy.
questions: How do I run a long ad hoc command in the background?
How do I check on a background ansible job later?
What do -B and -P mean for the ansible command?
What happens when the async timeout runs out?
Can I copy a big file in the background with async?
How do I start async jobs on many hosts quickly?

answer_card.title: Asynchronous ad hoc tasks
answer_card.answer_md:
Run in the background with a 3600 s limit and no polling:
```bash
ansible all -B 3600 -P 0 -a "/usr/bin/long_running_operation --do-stuff"
```
Check it later with the returned job ID:
```bash
ansible web1.example.com -m async_status -a "jid=488359678239.2844"
```
Or poll automatically, e.g. run up to 30 min and poll every 60 s:
```bash
ansible all -B 1800 -P 60 -a "/usr/bin/long_running_operation --do-stuff"
```
All jobs start before polling begins; use a high `--forks` to start them quickly. When the `-B` limit expires, the remote process is terminated. Async suits long shell commands and software upgrades; running `copy` async does not give a background transfer.
